correctness.rationale: For a feasible equilibrium the Jacobian is similar to minus D^(1/2)(I+tau A)D^(1/2), so strict stability is equivalent to matrix positive definiteness. Exact determinant/Cramer identities give rho (root 1-2t-t²+t³) for G0 and sigma=(sqrt17-1)/8 for G1. G1 positive definiteness at t=2/5 follows from six positive exact leading principal minors, and convex interpolation controls earlier t. The four five-vertex threshold witnesses use exact Cramer and principal-minor certificates; the independent finite graph scan covers every labeled connected graph of order at most five. The final verify.py was executed successfully. The proof asserts no unbounded enumeration or post-threshold dynamics.

value.rationale: A 2026 mathematical-ecology study argues from numerical and empirical ensembles that network clustering is associated with stronger competitive coexistence. A sharp counterexample to pointwise local monotonicity determines a concrete boundary of that inference, and proves six is the first possible connected species count. The counterexample preserves all degrees, requires only one standard two-edge switch, has exact algebraic thresholds and an exhaustive minimality certificate; it is motivated structurally rather than selected as an arbitrary parameter slice.
